reason: I want to build the pump, and heart muscle appears to fit the chamber's pumping walls.

reason: Add the pacemaker cells to give the muscular pump a rhythm.

reason: Join the arteries and veins to the capillaries to build the exchange route and return path.

reaction: The arrows and thin-wall inset make the route and exchange site clear.
reason: This is the only available combination, and it should make the oxygen-carrying cells needed for the blood route.
expectation: Hemoglobin will fit inside the flexible envelopes to form red blood cells that can carry oxygen.

effect: The red blood cells are made, and I learned they can make ATP from sugar without mitochondria.
reaction: That difference from the muscle cells was interesting.
reason: This is the only available combination; adding the cells to plasma should make blood for the vessel circuit.

effect: The red blood cells are now suspended in plasma as oxygen-carrying blood, ready to enter the vessel circuit.
reaction: The inset clarifies that blood includes other components too.
reason: This is the only available combination, and it should put the blood into the connected vessels.

effect: The blood now fills the vessel circuit, and the new goal is to put it into circulation.
reaction: The picture makes it clear that small substances cross capillary walls while red blood cells stay inside.
reason: This is the only available combination, and connecting the heart to the blood-filled circuit should make the blood circulate.
expectation: The beating heart will pump blood through the vessels and back to the heart.

effect: The heart and blood-filled vessels now form a closed circulation serving tissues, completing the chapter's goals.
reaction: Seeing the separate pump and vessel route come together was satisfying.

mostWorthwhile.text: Making red blood cells was most worthwhile because it showed how their energy supply differs from muscle cells: they make ATP from sugar without mitochondria.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding red blood cells to plasma felt straightforward, with little new to decide, though the inset acknowledged other blood components.

surprise.text: I was interested that the heart starts its own beat while nerves can adjust its rhythm.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, although the later choices were often the only available combinations.

continue.text: Yes. I would be interested to see how circulation connects with other body systems, especially after learning how red blood cells differ from muscle cells.
